lesson_title: One Workshop, Two Uniforms: the Production Possibility Curve
hook_text: One room of sewing machines. Two uniforms. The whole economy — explained.
clip_script: A small workshop: one room of machines, three machinists, one working day. All shirts: 60. All jerseys: 60. Mix them — and every dozen jerseys is PAID FOR in shirts. The day is fixed; push one up, the other comes down. Draw the possible days and you get a boundary — the edge of the possible. Now the three kinds of day. The FULL day: machines humming — ON the line, a maximum. The LAZY day: a machinist off sick, a machine jammed — INSIDE the line. The workshop didn't shrink; it just didn't use what it had. For a country, inside the line is unemployment's address. The DREAM day — 60 shirts AND 48 jerseys? BEYOND the line. Impossible — until the owner buys two more machines, and the whole boundary steps outward. That's growth. And the sharpest lesson: a country with millions of idle hands doesn't need new machines first. Its cheapest growth is walking back to the line — employing what it already has.
visual_style: A dawn workshop: garments stacking into plotted points, the boundary sweeping through them; three days flashing as dots on, inside and beyond the line; new machines rolling in as the boundary breathes outward; final shot of hands returning to the machines.
mood: Workshop craft warmth building into a national insight.
pacing: Steady stitch-by-stitch build through the menu, three clean point-beats, expansive ending.
